# Data tables (DT)

This is the short form. Before writing code in this area, read the full rules with reasons, bad/good examples and checks: `.ui-polish/rules/17-data-tables.md`.

- **DT-01 Tables are real tables** (warning). Tabular data uses `<table>` with a `<caption>` (or `aria-labelledby`), a `<thead>` of `<th scope="col">` cells and a `<tbody>`. The first cell of each row is a `<th scope="row">` when it names the row (a person, an invoice number). Never build a table from `<div>`s with grid or flex: screen readers lose the column headers.
- **DT-02 Columns are aligned by what they hold** (warning). Text and identifiers align to the start; numbers, money, percentages and durations align to the end with `tabular-nums`; dates use one fixed format; status is a short badge (text plus colour, never colour alone); row actions sit in the last column, aligned to the end. Each header aligns the same way as its column. Units go in the header ("Amount (USD)"), not in every cell.
- **DT-03 Sorting is visible and announced** (warning). A sortable column header contains a `<button>` with the column name (not "Sort"), followed by a decorative direction icon. The sorted column's `<th>` carries `aria-sort="ascending"` or `"descending"`, and only that one. The first click sorts ascending, the next reverses. Text sorts with `Intl.Collator`; numbers and dates sort by their raw value, never by the formatted string. Keep sort, filter and page in the URL (NV-06).
- **DT-04 The header stays and rows have a set density** (info). Tables taller than the screen keep the header visible (`position: sticky` on the header cells, with a background), and wide tables keep the first column sticky too. Pick one row height for the product (compact 36px, default 44px, comfortable 52px) and use it everywhere; do not mix. Rows show hover; zebra stripes only if rows are wider than about 1,000px.
- **DT-05 Every table has its states** (error). Loading shows skeleton rows with the real columns and widths (ST-02), not a spinner over an empty box. Empty has two forms (ST-03): nothing yet (explain and offer the create action) and no results for this filter (say which filter and offer to clear it). An error replaces the body with what failed and a retry (ST-04). While refetching, keep the old rows and show progress.
- **DT-06 Paging shows where you are** (warning). Paginated tables show the range and total ("21–40 of 340"), previous and next buttons that are disabled at the ends, and a page-size choice when pages are long. Filters, search and sort sit above the table, show how many rows match, and can be cleared in one click. Infinite scroll is for feeds, not for tables people compare or return to.
- **DT-07 Selection and row actions are predictable** (warning). Selectable rows have a checkbox column with a header checkbox (indeterminate when some are selected), and a bar that appears with the count and the bulk actions ("3 selected · Archive · Delete"). Per-row actions go in the last column: one or two visible buttons, the rest in a "More actions" menu labelled with the row ("More actions for INV-2041"). If the whole row opens a detail page, the row's first cell is a real link so it works from the keyboard and with middle-click.
- **DT-08 Long and missing values are handled** (info). Columns have a minimum width; long text truncates to one line with the full value available on hover and focus (a Tooltip, not `title`), except the row's name column, which wraps. Missing values show an en dash with an accessible "Not set", never blank, "null", "undefined" or "NaN". Identifiers and emails never wrap mid-word.
